answer:
**Four option groups switch zgrep to the sorted/ordered path without `--sort`:**

- **`--exec` / `--execute`** — needs to know *which* files matched, which only the ordered path tracks; it also forces quiet mode (`src/main.zig:2226`, `src/main.zig:2237`).
- **`--heading`** — streaming emits in completion order, so per-file groups would interleave and headers point at the wrong cluster (`src/main.zig:2231`, `src/main.zig:2227-2230`). Aliases that set it: `--group-by-file` (`src/main.zig:1309`), `--pretty` (`src/main.zig:1313-1317`), `-p` (`src/main.zig:1572-1576`).
- **`--pre`** — runs per file, so it needs the ordered path (`src/main.zig:2233`).
- **`--queries-file`** (batch) — injects `--sort` into every query's argv (`src/main.zig:1961`).

Additionally, **more than one explicit FILE operand** forces the ordered path to keep GNU argument order (`src/main.zig:2402`).

Note: `-k`/`--kamikaze`/`--dataflow` clear `sort` (`src/main.zig:989-991`, `src/main.zig:1642-1645`), but the exec/heading/pre checks run after parsing (`src/main.zig:2226-2233`), so they win.
